channel.title: Ascent Vision: Answers
channel.description: Plain answers to the questions business owners ask about SEO, GEO and AI answers, lead tracking and websites.

item.title: Who owns software that was built for your business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Under US copyright law, the person who writes software is usually its author. See what must be in writing for you to own it and what to ask for.

item.title: What should you have ready before hiring a software developer?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A checklist for owners before hiring a software developer: the job it must do, who uses it, what it connects to, its data, and who owns accounts.

item.title: What should you ask before hiring someone to build AI for your business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Questions to put to anyone who offers to build AI for your business: ownership, where your data goes, human review, the off switch, testing and upkeep.

item.title: What does it take to keep custom software running after launch?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Custom software needs updates, hosting renewals, tested backups, accounts in your name, alerts when it breaks, notes and a written change agreement.

item.title: What can a small business realistically automate with AI?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A plain map of the tasks a small business can hand to AI and automation, such as routing and reminders, and the ones that still need a person's judgment.

item.title: Should a person approve what an AI system sends to customers?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Keep a person reviewing AI messages at the start and on anything risky. See when relaxing review is reasonable, what to check first and what to log.

item.title: How do you tell if a task is worth automating?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A six-question test for any task: how often it repeats, how many steps, how fixed they are, what a mistake costs, who approves and how you would notice.

item.title: How do you stop an AI assistant from making things up?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: You cannot make it impossible, but you can reduce it. Owner-level steps: approved facts only, permission to say I don't know, limits, handoff and testing.

item.title: How do you check a developer's work before paying for more?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Split the project into stages, write plain-words checks first, watch each stage work on your real examples, and know what to do when a stage fails.

item.title: Should you buy off-the-shelf software or have something built?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Should you buy ready-made software or have something built? A plain decision test for owners, including the honest case for trying a bought product first.

item.title: What should you expect in the first months after hiring an SEO or GEO agency?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The first three months with an SEO or GEO agency: what you should receive and when, what the agency needs from you, and what is too early to judge.

item.title: What is white-label SEO, and does it matter if your agency outsources the work?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What white-label SEO means for the business paying for it, when outsourced work is fine, and the questions that show who actually does it.

item.title: What is online reputation management, and is it worth paying for?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What reputation management services sell, the parts an owner can do alone, and the FTC and Google rules that close off the shortcuts some offer.

item.title: What is offline conversion tracking, and should a service business use it?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What it means to send your won jobs back to Google Ads, what Google says it measures, and when a small service business should bother with it.

item.title: What is call tracking, and can it hurt your Google listing?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What call tracking numbers do, what Google asks of the phone number on your profile, and what to settle before a vendor rents you a number.

item.title: What is a zero-click search, and what does it mean for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What a zero-click search is, what Pew measured about AI summaries and clicks, and why a call from your Google profile can be a zero-click win.

item.title: Should you hire a marketing consultant or a marketing agency?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The difference between paying for advice and paying for the work, when a marketing consultant suits a small service business, and when an agency does.

item.title: Is advertising on Yelp worth it for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Yelp Ads charge for, whether paying changes your reviews, the contract terms to check, and how to judge Yelp by the jobs it actually sends you.

item.title: Why are my leads low quality, and how do you get better ones?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Why one source sends wrong-fit leads, and the fixes on the source side: who you reach, what you promise, how easy the form is and what you count.

item.title: How much does a website cost for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What decides the cost of a small business website, the running costs owners forget, and how to compare quotes, without a price list.

item.title: How many Google reviews does a business need?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Google says about reviews and local results, what customers told BrightLocal about review counts and recency, and a target you can keep up.

item.title: What does Florida's law on sales calls and texts mean for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Florida's telephone solicitation law and Telemarketing Act say about sales calls and texts: consent, calling hours, stop requests and the state list.

item.title: Will AI assistants replace Google search?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: No one can say. Google puts AI answers inside Search, and Pew found many U.S. adults read AI summaries and use chatbots to look things up.

item.title: Why did Facebook unpublish or limit your business Page, and how do you appeal?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Why Meta takes down or limits a Facebook business Page, how to appeal from the Page, and what an unpublished Page loses, from messages to running ads.

item.title: Why was my Google or Facebook ad rejected or disapproved?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Why Google and Meta reject single ads, where each shows the reason, and how to fix the ad and ask for a review instead of posting the same ad again.

item.title: Why is my website down, and what should I check first?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The owner's order of checks when a business website will not load: you or everyone, the domain, the hosting, a recent change, a hack, an outage.

item.title: Why is my website's contact form not sending me emails?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The owner's test for a contact form that has gone quiet, the usual causes you can check yourself, and a backup so no inquiry is lost meanwhile.

item.title: Why has my small business stopped growing?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A plain diagnosis for a service business that has stalled: flat inquiries, leads that do not become jobs, a full calendar, or fading repeat work.

item.title: Why did your business email stop working, and what do you check first?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The usual reasons business email stops arriving, the order to check them in, who to call, and how to keep a website move from cutting off your email.

item.title: Why did my website traffic drop, and should I worry?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A drop in website visits usually has an ordinary cause: the season, a change to the site, a Google update. How to check each in order and when it matters.

item.title: When should a new business start marketing, and what comes first?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Start before opening day with the basics customers need to find and reach you, use Google's opening date, then track where your first customers come from.

item.title: What should a service business put on its business card, and are digital cards worth it?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The few lines a service business card needs, what to leave off, how to add a QR code people will trust, and where digital cards fit.

item.title: What should you do if your Google Ads account is hacked or shows charges you did not make?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Secure the Google Account first, check Google Ads and your card statements for changes you did not make, then ask Google to review the account.

item.title: What should you do if your Facebook business page is hacked?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What to do when someone takes over your Facebook business Page: Meta's recovery form, what to check while you wait, and how to lock the Page down after.

item.title: What should you do if your business email account is hacked?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The first-hour steps when a business inbox is taken over, from Google's and Microsoft's own guidance, then who to warn and where to report it.

item.title: What should a small business do if it gets an ADA website demand letter or lawsuit?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Do not ignore an ADA website demand letter and do not pay before a lawyer reads it. What to keep, what the Justice Department says, and what to fix.

item.title: What should you check before a new website goes live?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A small business website checklist for launch: test every phone link and form, check the details, keep old addresses working and own the logins.

item.title: What reading level should a small business website be written at?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: No single grade fits every business website. Write for your actual readers in short, plain sentences, and treat a readability score as a check.

item.title: What is Meta Business Suite, and how is it different from Business Manager and Ads Manager?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Meta says Business Suite is for, why Business Manager is now called a business portfolio, and when an owner needs Ads Manager instead.

item.title: What is GoHighLevel, and does a small business need it?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What HighLevel says its software does, why agencies run client leads on it, and the ownership and export questions to ask before yours does.

item.title: What is Ask Maps in Google Maps, and what does it mean for a local business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Ask Maps lets people ask Google Maps detailed questions about places. What Google says it draws on, where it works and what a business owner controls.

item.title: What is an AI agent, and should a small business use one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: An AI agent is software that decides its own steps toward a goal. What that means for an owner, what to keep a person on, and what to ask a seller.

item.title: What is a tracking pixel, and does a service business's website need one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What a tracking pixel is, why ad platforms ask for one, what it sends to a third party, and why health pages carry extra risk under federal guidance.

item.title: What is a marketing calendar, and what goes on one for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A marketing calendar puts your year on one page: busy and slow months, holiday hours, seasonal pushes, review dates and renewals you cannot afford to miss.

item.title: What is a lead magnet, and does a service business need one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A lead magnet is a free checklist, guide or estimate offered for contact details. When it helps a service business, what to ask, and keeping the promise.

item.title: What is a Google core update, and what should an owner do after one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Google's core updates are broad changes made several times a year. Why a drop after one is usually not a penalty, and what an owner should do first.

item.title: What is a good cost per lead for a small service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: No outside average fits every trade. Work out the most a lead is worth to you from your close rate and a typical job, then judge ads by jobs won.

item.title: What is a favicon, and does a small business website need one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The small icon in a browser tab and beside your site's name on Google: what it is, what Google asks of it, how it fits your logo, and when to check it.

item.title: What is a drip campaign, and does a small service business need one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A drip campaign in plain words, the few a service business might use, when one hurts more than it helps, and the email rules every message follows.

item.title: What is a CMS, and what are plugins on a website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A content management system in plain words, the two kinds owners usually meet, what plugins are, and why each one needs updates and an owner.

item.title: What is a brand style guide, and does a small business need one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A one-page brand style guide for a small business: logo files, colors, fonts, the name and the tone, plus readable colors and who keeps the files.

item.title: What happens when your website's security certificate expires?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What visitors see when a site's security certificate lapses, who usually renews it, and why renewals are coming more often as certificate lifetimes shrink.

item.title: What does Google mean by 'helpful, people-first' content?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Google's people-first content guide in plain terms: the questions it asks, the warning signs it lists, what E-E-A-T stands for and what owners can take.

item.title: What do customer acquisition cost, ROI and ROAS mean in a marketing report?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Customer acquisition cost, ROI and ROAS in plain words, with one worked example, why ROAS can look good while you lose money, and what to ask.

item.title: What counts as a conversion in Google Ads, and why does it not match your new customers?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A Google Ads conversion is whatever action the account is set to count, such as a call or form. Why that is not your customer count, and what to ask.

item.title: What can you claim in your ads: 'best', 'guaranteed', 'lowest price', or naming a competitor?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The FTC's ad basics for a small service business: proof before an ad runs, 'number one' and price claims, guarantees, free offers and naming competitors.

item.title: What are vanity metrics, and which numbers should a small business care about?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Vanity metrics such as followers, likes and raw visits look good but do not show whether customers came. Here is what each one hides and what to watch.

item.title: What are the different parts of a Google results page?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A plain map of a Google results page: which parts are paid ads and which are earned, from map results and AI Overviews to the ordinary links.

item.title: Do you need a web designer or a web developer?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A web designer shapes how a site looks and guides visitors; a developer builds and runs it. Which one a service business usually needs, and what to ask.

item.title: Should a business use a TikTok business account or a personal or creator account?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What TikTok's Verified Business Account adds and gives up compared with a General account, how switching works, and who should hold the login.

item.title: What can you do if someone registered a domain with your business name?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How to tell a squatter from a fair claim, the two routes to a domain that uses your name (ICANN's dispute policy and federal court), and what to do first.

item.title: What can you do if someone is using your business name online?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How to tell an impostor from a business with the same name, what the FTC's impersonation rule covers, and the steps that usually help. Not legal advice.

item.title: Should a service business put its cancellation and refund policy on its website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Why a short cancellation and refund policy where people book prevents arguments, how to word it, and what the FTC's Cooling-Off Rule covers.

item.title: Should a new business put up a coming soon page, and what should it say?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When a coming soon page helps a new business and when it hurts, what to put on it, how builders handle one, and when to replace it with a real site.

item.title: Should your business have a Wikipedia page?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Usually not. What Wikipedia asks of a company, why owners are told not to write their own article, and what paid page-writing offers leave out.

item.title: Should you let Meta's AI assistant or an auto-reply answer your Facebook and Instagram messages?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Meta's inbox auto-replies and its business AI agent do, where each helps or hurts a service business, and how every message still becomes a lead.

item.title: Should a small business use AI to make its ads, videos or phone greeting?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: AI can draft ads and image variations a person checks, but never invent customers or results. What Google Ads, Meta and the FTC say about AI-made ads.

item.title: Should a service business send customers a thank-you note after the job?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Why a short thank-you after the job is worth sending, whether to use a card, text or email, what to say in two lines, and when the email rules apply.

item.title: Should you post on Reddit or forums to show up in AI answers?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Google and OpenAI have Reddit data deals, but Reddit's rules and the FTC both draw lines on hidden promotion. What an owner should know before posting.

item.title: Should you pay other websites to link to yours?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: No. Google treats buying links to lift rankings as link spam. What its policy says, when a paid link is fine, and how to read a link-package pitch.

item.title: Should my website have a separate page for every town I serve?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Usually not near-identical ones. Google's spam policies list city pages that funnel visitors to one page as doorway abuse. How to read a town-page pitch.

item.title: Should customers be able to text your business, and how do you set that up?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Why a text line on the business number can catch more inquiries, how to set it up, who should answer, and what consent covers a reply.

item.title: Should a service business take payments on its website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When taking payments online helps a service business, when a call and a quote should come first, and how to keep card details off your own web pages.

item.title: Should a home-based business show its home address on its website, Facebook page and listings?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Usually not. What Google says about hiding a home address, what a Facebook Page needs, and the FTC's postal-address option for commercial email.

item.title: Should a service business start a Facebook group, or just keep a page?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How Meta compares Facebook Pages and groups, when a group suits a service business, the time it takes, and why joining local groups is often enough.

item.title: What is the difference between a lead, a prospect and a qualified lead?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Plain definitions of a lead, a prospect and a qualified lead for a service business, plus warm and cold leads and what to ask when a report counts leads.

item.title: Is WordPress a good choice for a small business website?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: WordPress.org against WordPress.com, what WordPress gives a small business, the upkeep it asks for, and who it usually suits. Upkeep matters most.

item.title: Is Valpak advertising worth it for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Valpak says it sells, how a shared coupon mailer differs from your own mailing, and how to judge it by booked jobs and tracked codes. No prices.

item.title: Is text message marketing worth it for a service business, and what consent does it need?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Where marketing texts help a service business and where they annoy, the consent the FCC and the wireless industry describe, and how to count results.

item.title: Is sponsoring a local team, school or event worth it for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Sponsoring a youth team, school or event can build goodwill. How to choose one, what to ask for, how to trace the inquiries it brings, and a tax note.

item.title: Is marketing tax deductible for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What the IRS small-business tax guide says about deducting advertising, the costs owners often mix up, and the records to keep. A plain summary.

item.title: Is advertising in a local magazine or newspaper worth it for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When a community magazine or local paper suits a service business, what to ask the publisher, how to trace the ad, and the FTC's truth-in-ads basics.

item.title: Is it legal for a small business to use an AI voice to call customers or leads?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The FCC's 2024 ruling treats AI-generated voices as artificial under the TCPA, so calls need consent. What that means for an owner calling leads.

item.title: Is Houzz Pro worth it for a contractor or designer?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Houzz Pro is, how its free plan, paid plans and advertising differ, which trades it tends to suit, and what to check before you sign up.

item.title: Is Groupon worth it for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How Groupon works for a service business, who a voucher deal can suit, the limits to set first, and why repeat customers are the real test.

item.title: Is the GoDaddy website builder good enough for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What GoDaddy says its builders do, how domain and site are kept apart, and what to check about ownership and leaving later. No prices or ranking.

item.title: Is field service software like Jobber or Housecall Pro worth it for a small service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What field service software like Jobber and Housecall Pro says it does, the marketing parts, and what to check before you sign. No ranking or prices.

item.title: Is door-to-door marketing worth it for a service business, and what rules apply?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When knocking on doors can pay off for a service business, what it really costs, Florida's home solicitation permit and cancel rules, and how to track it.

item.title: Is Bark worth it for finding customers?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How Bark's credits work for professionals, what to check before you buy them, and how to judge Bark by the jobs you actually win from it.

item.title: Is a Google virtual tour or 360 photo shoot worth it for a small business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A Google virtual tour can suit a showroom, studio or venue that customers visit. It rarely suits work done at the customer's home. Photos come first.

item.title: Should a business use an Instagram creator account or a business account?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What Instagram says each professional account type is for, which one a service business usually wants, what changes when you switch, and who holds it.

item.title: What is the difference between inbound and outbound marketing, and which suits a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Inbound marketing gets you found; outbound reaches out first. How that differs from traditional vs digital, the rules on calls and email, and which fits.

item.title: How do you write a short business bio for Instagram, Facebook and your Google profile?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Write one short business bio from four plain facts, then trim it for Instagram, Facebook and Google. What Google's rules allow, plus three examples.

item.title: How do you tell customers you are closed for a holiday, vacation or storm?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Put one closed message everywhere customers check: Google, the website, voicemail, email and social. Say when you reopen and who to call if it is urgent.

item.title: How do you tell customers about a price increase without losing them?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Give notice before the change, tell regulars first, state the date and what stays the same, honor quotes already given, and answer pushback calmly.

item.title: How do you spot official-looking scam letters sent to small businesses?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Directory bills, fake trademark notices and government-style demands: the signs the FTC and USPTO name, how to check, and where to report.

item.title: How do you say no to a customer politely?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A simple pattern for turning down a discount, extra work, a date you cannot make or a job you do not do, with sample lines for each case.

item.title: How should a small business respond to a BBB complaint?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What the BBB does with a complaint, how long a business is given to answer, and a calm three-part reply, plus why leaving it unanswered usually costs more.

item.title: How do you choose a name for a service business?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: A good business name is easy to say and spell and leaves room to grow. The official checks to run first: state records, trademark search and web address.

item.title: How do you market a service business in a small town?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What changes when your market is a small town, and the basics that usually matter most: being easy to find, reviews, referrals and showing up locally.

item.title: How do you market a mobile or home-based service business with no storefront?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Without a storefront, show where you go instead of where you are: a service-area profile on Google, a clear website, a recognizable vehicle and referrals.

item.title: How do you make a website easy for older customers to read and use?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What W3C's guidance on older web users points to: text that enlarges, strong contrast, clear links, time and simple forms, plus phone checks.

item.title: How does a service business get more repeat customers?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: The habits that bring service customers back, how to run a maintenance plan or membership honestly, and how to count repeat work.

item.title: How does a service business get commercial clients instead of only homeowners?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Business buyers often want proof and paperwork before price. How commercial clients differ, where to find them and what government work needs.

item.title: How do you stop working with a difficult customer without a fight or a bad review?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When ending work with a customer is the right call, how to do it calmly, a sample message, and what the FTC's review rule means if a bad review follows.

item.title: How do you get a second location on Google when your business opens another one?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: When a second place earns its own Google Business Profile, what each location needs, and why a new profile usually starts fresh. Moves are different.

item.title: How much website traffic should a small business get?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Why no single traffic number fits a service business, the comparisons that say more, and what Google Analytics' peer benchmarks can show.

item.title: How do plumbers get more leads?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Plumbers usually win leads by answering the emergency call, weighing paid options and keeping free ones sound. Includes Florida's license number rule.

item.title: How do photographers get clients?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Photographers usually win clients with a portfolio page per kind of work, visual platforms, a hidden-address Google profile and a form that asks the date.

item.title: How do personal trainers and fitness coaches get clients online?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Trainers usually get found on Instagram and convert on a website with an application and a page per kind of client, keeping public claims on firm ground.

item.title: How do HVAC companies get leads?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: HVAC leads follow the weather. How a maintenance-plan page, Local Services Ads, commercial bids, dealer locators and lead companies fit, judged by jobs.

item.title: How do accountants and bookkeepers get clients?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: Accountants and bookkeepers usually grow by referral first, then directories, and adjust the website around tax season. Includes Florida's CPA title rule.

item.title: What is the difference between an estimate and a quote, and is a quote binding?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: How the words estimate and quote are usually used, why the written terms matter more than the label, and when a quote can become a binding contract.

item.title: Does a small business website need an accessibility statement?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What an accessibility statement is, what W3C suggests it include, what it cannot do on its own, and why a working way to report problems matters most.

item.title: Should a small business get a separate phone line, such as VoIP, instead of using a personal cell?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
item.description: What a separate business line or an internet phone (VoIP) service adds, the trade-offs the FCC lists, and the questions to ask a provider first.

item.title: Does a small business website in the US need a cookie banner?
item.dc:creator: Ascent Vision
